record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: What is the exact computational complexity class of the two-dimensional PEPS zero-testing problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on a two-dimensional square lattice of size $N\times N$ is defined as follows. To each site $(i,j)$ of the lattice associate a tensor $A^{(i,j)}_{s; l,r,u,d}$ with a physical index $s\in\{1,\dots,d\}$ and four virtual indices $l,r,u,d\in\{1,\dots,D\}$ (with appropriate boundary conditions, e.g., fixed boundary virtual indices). The PEPS is the vector
$$|\Psi\rangle \;=\; \sum_{\{s_{i,j}\}} \mathrm{tTr}\!\left(\bigotimes_{i,j} A^{(i,j)}_{s_{i,j}}\right)\, |s_{1,1}\dots s_{N,N}\rangle \;\in\; (\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes N^2},$$
where $\mathrm{tTr}$ denotes contraction of all matching virtual indices according to the lattice adjacency.

The 2D PEPS zero-testing problem is the following decision problem: given as input a collection of tensors $\{A^{(i,j)}\}$ (with rational or algebraic entries) and a lattice size $N$, decide whether the resulting PEPS vector $|\Psi\rangle$ is the zero vector.

Determine the exact computational complexity class of this decision problem. It is known that the problem is NP-hard (already for tensors that are homogeneous in the bulk with a chosen boundary), but precise containment in a known complexity class matching this lower bound has not been established. The task is to characterize the problem's complexity exactly (i.e., prove completeness for some standard complexity class).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is known to be NP-hard, with a related variant proven undecidable, but the exact complexity class for 2D PEPS zero-testing remains open as of recent literature. Subsequent work (e.g., 2025 work on injective PEPS) addresses related but distinct restrictions, not pinning down the exact class for the general 2D zero-testing problem.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Question on the exact complexity class of 2D PEPS zero-testing posed as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The exact computational complexity class of 2D PEPS zero-testing is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of PEPS zero testing
status_evidence.snippet: Zero-testing of PEPS is proven NP-hard for homogeneous bulk PEPS with boundary; a variation is undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: NP-hardness is established but exact class is not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses complexity of zero-testing for injective PEPS, a restricted class.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress targets restricted subclasses, leaving the general 2D case open.
